record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: Can Taylor expansion around zero chemical potential determine the QCD equation of state and, more importantly, identify phase transitions or the QCD critical point when only low-order coefficients are practically accessible and the convergence near the transition region is slow? This includes the open issue of whether sufficiently accurate higher-order coefficients can be computed to make the method reliable beyond very small chemical potential.

evidence.quote: In principle, cn can be calculated for any n, but as n becomes larger, the expression becomes more complicated, and the calculation is practically hard because the statistical error increases. At present, only low-order terms have been calculated.

With the Taylor expansion method, although it is difficult to investigate a large area of µ, for small µ it is possible to perform high-precision calculations on the same level as ordinary lattice QCD simulations since the calculation method is the same as the ordinary lattice QCD simulation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) on a four-dimensional Euclidean lattice with quark chemical potential $\mu$, and let $p(T,\mu)$ denote the pressure (equation of state) as a function of temperature $T$ and $\mu$. Because the fermion determinant becomes complex for $\mu 
eq 0$, direct Monte Carlo sampling suffers from a sign problem. The Taylor expansion method approximates the equation of state via
$$\frac{p(T,\mu)}{T^4} \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_{n}(T)\,\Big(\frac{\mu}{T}\Big)^{n},$$
where the coefficients $c_n(T)$ are computed at $\mu=0$ as expectation values of products of derivatives of $\ln\det M(\mu)$ (with $M$ the lattice Dirac operator). In practice only low-order coefficients $c_n$ (currently up to about $n=8$) can be evaluated, since the statistical variance of the stochastic estimators of $c_n$ grows rapidly with $n$, and the radius of convergence of the series is expected to shrink near a phase transition or a putative QCD critical point in the $(T,\mu)$ plane.

Problem. Determine whether the Taylor expansion of the QCD equation of state around $\mu=0$ can, with only practically accessible low-order coefficients $\{c_n\}_{n\le N}$ (for moderate $N$), reliably (i) reconstruct the equation of state $p(T,\mu)/T^4$ in a neighborhood of the chiral/deconfinement transition, and (ii) detect and locate phase transitions and the QCD critical point. In particular, establish whether sufficiently accurate higher-order Taylor coefficients $c_n(T)$ can be computed by lattice methods so as to extend the reliable range of the expansion beyond the regime $\mu/T \ll 1$, or alternatively prove obstructions (e.g., from the location of Lee–Yang singularities and the finite radius of convergence) that preclude such reconstruction near the transition region.
artifact.status_search_result: The Taylor expansion approach to finite-density lattice QCD remains an active area of research as of 2025–2026. Higher-order coefficients (through eighth order) have been computed by the HotQCD and Wuppertal–Budapest collaborations, and methods based on Padé/conformal resummations and Lee–Yang zero analyses are being developed, but a definitive determination of the QCD critical point or the equation of state at moderate-to-large $\mu/T$ has not been achieved. The fundamental obstruction—rapid growth of statistical error in higher-order coefficients and a possibly limited radius of convergence near the transition—is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: HotQCD: Taylor expansions and Padé approximants for cumulants of conserved charges
status_evidence.snippet: We present results on Taylor expansions of cumulants of conserved charge fluctuations up to eighth order... and discuss limitations near the chiral crossover.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order Taylor coefficients are being computed but their accuracy and the convergence near the transition remain limiting factors.

status_evidence.title: Lattice QCD equation of state at finite chemical potential from an alternative expansion scheme
status_evidence.snippet: We propose an alternative expansion scheme... extending the reach of lattice QCD beyond what direct Taylor expansion permits.
status_evidence.claim: Researchers continue to develop alternatives because direct Taylor expansion's reliable range in $\mu/T$ is restricted.
